faq.q: What does Ayaan mean in this record?
faq.a: This entry records Arabic عيان (ʿiyān), with the sense “visible,” “evident” or “in plain sight.”

faq.q: Is Ayaan always an Arabic name?
faq.a: No. Ayaan is a Latin-script spelling used in more than one naming context; origin depends on the intended language, script and pronunciation.

faq.q: How is Ayaan written in Arabic here?
faq.a: The form used by this record is عيان.

faq.q: Does Ayaan have one universally agreed meaning?
faq.a: No. The same Latin spelling can represent different words in different languages. This page documents only the Arabic form عيان.

faq.q: Is Ayaan a Qur’anic personal name?
faq.a: This entry does not claim Ayaan/عيان as a Qur’anic personal name.
The Arabic form can be approximated as “ʿi-yān”; English-speaking families may pronounce the Latin spelling differently.

faq.q: Is Ayaan used for boys or girls?
faq.a: This dataset records Ayaan as unisex, but practice varies by country and family; no registration statistics are claimed.

faq.q: What should parents verify before choosing Ayaan?
faq.a: Confirm the intended language, script and pronunciation, because the same Latin spelling can represent different names.
